literal: The barbarians went to court to sue him for severity and asked for the former inspector Kou Zuli.
idiomatic: Barbarians sued at court for his harsh rule and asked for former inspector Kou Zuli.

literal: When seventy garrison soldiers were sent to escort Daoyuan back to the capital, both men were dismissed from office.
idiomatic: Seventy garrison soldiers escorted Daoyuan to the capital; both were dismissed.

literal: Later he was made Intendant of Henan.
idiomatic: Later he was Intendant of Henan.

literal: Emperor Ming changed the garrisons Woye, Huaishuo, Bogulv, Wuchuan, Fuming, Rouxuan, Huaihuang, and Yuyi all to provinces, their commanderies, counties, and garrison names to follow ancient cities and towns.
idiomatic: Ming turned garrisons Woye, Huaishuo, Bogulv, Wuchuan, Fuming, Rouxuan, Huaihuang, and Yuyi into provinces, naming counties and posts after ancient towns.

literal: Daoyuan was ordered with staff as Concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant, traveling post-haste with Grand Commander Li Chong to plan establishment and cut or retain posts.
idiomatic: He was ordered Concurrent Yellow Gate Attendant to ride post-haste with Grand Commander Li Chong to plan posts and cuts.

literal: The garrisons rebelled; he returned without accomplishing it.
idiomatic: Garrisons rebelled; he returned without result.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang troops were sent to attack Yangzhou; Inspector Yuan Faseng also rebelled at Pengcheng.
idiomatic: In early Xiaochang troops attacked Yangzhou; Inspector Yuan Faseng rebelled at Pengcheng.

literal: Daoyuan was ordered with staff, Concurrent Palace Attendant, and acting Mobile Secretariat Director to command the armies, following Vice Director Li Ping's precedent.
idiomatic: He was ordered with staff, Concurrent Palace Attendant, acting Mobile Secretariat Director, commanding armies after Li Ping's precedent.

literal: The army reached Guoyang and was defeated and withdrew.
idiomatic: The army reached Guoyang, was beaten, and withdrew.

literal: Daoyuan pursued and beheaded many.
idiomatic: Daoyuan pursued and took many heads.

literal: Later he was made Censor-in-Chief.
idiomatic: Later he was Censor-in-Chief.

literal: Daoyuan had always had the reputation of severity and fierceness; powerful families at first somewhat feared him.
idiomatic: Daoyuan had a name for severity; great houses at first feared him.

literal: Yet he could not correct wrongs; his reputation fell further.
idiomatic: Yet he could not correct abuses; his standing fell.

literal: Governor of Si Province, Prince of Runan Yuan Yue, favored his intimate Qiu Nian, who constantly slept and rose with him.
idiomatic: Si Governor, Prince of Runan Yuan Yue, favored Qiu Nian, who slept and rose with him.

literal: When choosing provincial officials, most came through Nian.
idiomatic: Choosing provincial officials mostly went through Nian.

literal: Nian often hid in Yue's residence and sometimes returned home; Daoyuan secretly learned of it and arrested Nian and put him in prison.
idiomatic: Nian hid in Yue's house and sometimes went home; Daoyuan learned secretly, arrested him, and jailed him.

literal: Yue petitioned Empress Ling to spare Nian's life; there was an edict pardoning him.
idiomatic: Yue petitioned Empress Ling to spare Nian; an edict pardoned him.

literal: Daoyuan then took his life and therefore impeached Yue.
idiomatic: Daoyuan then executed him and impeached Yue.

literal: At the time Inspector of Yong Xiao Baoyin's rebellion showed signs; Palace Attendant Prince of Chengyang Hui had long resented Daoyuan and therefore urged the court to send him as envoy to the west of the Pass.
idiomatic: Yong Inspector Xiao Baoyin's revolt showed signs; Palace Attendant Prince of Chengyang Hui, resenting Daoyuan, urged sending him as envoy west of the Pass.

literal: Baoyin feared Daoyuan would plot against him and sent his mobile secretariat gentleman Guo Zixia to surround Daoyuan at Yinpan Post Station.
idiomatic: Baoyin feared Daoyuan and sent secretariat gentleman Guo Zixia to surround him at Yinpan Post.

literal: The station lay below a hill; they regularly ate from the well below the hill.
idiomatic: The post lay below a hill; they drank from the hill's well.

literal: Once surrounded, they dug the well more than ten zhang and found no water.
idiomatic: Besieged, they dug the well ten-plus zhang deep and found no water.

literal: Water gone and strength spent, the bandits climbed the wall and entered.
idiomatic: Water gone, strength spent, rebels scaled the wall.

literal: Daoyuan, his younger brother Daolüe, and two sons were all killed.
idiomatic: Daoyuan, younger brother Daolüe, and two sons were all killed.

literal: Daoyuan glared and shouted at the bandits, dying with a fierce voice.
idiomatic: Daoyuan glared and cursed the rebels aloud, and died with his voice still fierce.

literal: Baoyin still sent men to gather father and sons and bury them east of Chang'an.
idiomatic: Baoyin still sent men to bury father and sons east of Chang'an.

literal: When affairs were settled the coffin returned; he was posthumously made Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Inspector of Ji, and Baron of Anding.
idiomatic: When order returned the coffin came home; he was posthumously Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Ji Inspector, Baron of Anding.

literal: The source text at this point is corrupt and unreadable.
idiomatic: The source text at this point is corrupt and unreadable.

literal: Daoyuan loved learning, read through strange books, and wrote a commentary on the Water Classic in forty scrolls and Basic Records in thirteen sections.
idiomatic: Daoyuan loved learning, read strange books, and wrote a commentary on the Water Classic in forty scrolls and Basic Records in thirteen sections.

literal: He also wrote Seven Missions and other pieces, all current in the world.
idiomatic: He also wrote Seven Missions and other works, all current in the world.

literal: Yet the brothers could not live in harmony and were much given to suspicion; opinion of the time slighted them.
idiomatic: Yet the brothers were not harmonious and much suspicious; opinion slighted them.

literal: His son Xiaoyou inherited.
idiomatic: Son Xiaoyou inherited.

literal: Daoyuan's fourth younger brother Daoshen, styled Shanji, ranged through historical records and had administrative capacity.
idiomatic: Fourth brother Daoshen, styled Shanji, ranged histories and had administrative gift.

literal: He held Administrator of Zhengping and had a name for ability.
idiomatic: He was Zhengping Administrator and had a name for ability.

literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of Changle.
idiomatic: He became Chancellor of Changle.

literal: At death he was posthumously made Inspector of Ping.
idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Ping Inspector.

literal: Daoshen's younger brother Daoyue, styled Shanli, was plain and slow, and quite loved zither and books.
idiomatic: Younger brother Daoyue, styled Shanli, was plain and slow, loving zither and books.

literal: By nature he made many visits and liked to plead for glory and profit; begging without end, he was often laughed at.
idiomatic: He made many calls and begged for rank and profit without end; men laughed at him.

literal: Hard pressed in the world, he could not escape hunger and cold.
idiomatic: Hard pressed in the world, he could not escape hunger and cold.

literal: Late in life he held the two commandery posts Donglai and Luoyang.
idiomatic: Late in life he held Donglai and Luoyang.

literal: His government was quiet and pure; officials and people were at peace.
idiomatic: Government was quiet; officials and people were at peace.

literal: Fan's younger brother Daojun's son Yun, styled Youhe.
idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Daojun's son Yun, styled Youhe.

literal: Fond of learning, he had literary talent and especially excelled in administrative work.
idiomatic: He loved learning, had literary gift, and excelled in administration.

literal: Presented as Outstanding Talent, he ranked high in the archery-and-policy examination.
idiomatic: Presented as Outstanding Talent, he ranked high in archery and policy.

literal: He held the post of Outer Troops Gentleman in the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was Outer Troops Gentleman in the Masters of Writing.

literal: Mobile Secretariat Chief Changsun Chengye drew him as secretariat gentleman.
idiomatic: Mobile Secretariat Chief Changsun Chengye made him secretariat gentleman.

literal: Yun also had martial gift and always aimed at merit and fame.
idiomatic: Yun also had martial gift and aimed at merit and fame.

literal: Whenever he offered plans to Chengye, most were adopted.
idiomatic: Plans offered to Chengye were mostly adopted.

literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Viscount of Weichang.
idiomatic: For merit he was Viscount of Weichang.

literal: Yun at the army memorialized to reduce his own rank and title and ask posthumous grant for his father; the edict made his father General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Inspector of An.
idiomatic: At the army Yun asked to cut his own rank for his father's posthumous grant; the edict made father General Who Punishes the Barbarians and An Inspector.

literal: Later Yun with Tangzhou Inspector Cui Yuanzhen firmly held Pingyang.
idiomatic: Later Yun with Tangzhou Inspector Cui Yuanzhen held Pingyang firm.

literal: Erzhu Rong raised troops to the capital; Yun and Yuanzhen would not follow and were killed when Rong's secretariat gentleman Fan Zigao took the city.
idiomatic: Erzhu Rong marched on the capital; Yun and Yuanzhen refused and were killed when Fan Zigao took the city.

literal: Writings he composed circulated fairly widely.
idiomatic: His writings circulated fairly widely.

literal: He drafted a book on the Murong house but did not finish.
idiomatic: He drafted a book on the Murong house but did not finish.

literal: His son Huaize was Chief Clerk for flowing affairs in the Ministry of Works.
idiomatic: Son Huaize was Chief Clerk for flowing affairs in the Ministry of Works.

literal: Han Xiu, styled Baiwu, was a man of Changli.
idiomatic: Han Xiu, styled Baiwu, came from Changli.

literal: His grandfather Zai was Chamberlain for Attendants under Murong Jun.
idiomatic: Grandfather Zai was Chamberlain for Attendants under Murong Jun.

literal: His father Jing, at the beginning of Huangshi, submitted to Wei and was made General Who Proclaims Might and Commandant of Cavalry.
idiomatic: Father Jing, at the start of Huangshi, submitted to Wei and was made General Who Proclaims Might and Cavalry Commandant.

literal: Xiu held posts in the Masters of Writing and was enfeoffed Viscount of Suichang.
idiomatic: Xiu served in the Masters of Writing and was Viscount of Suichang.

literal: Emperor Wencheng called Xiu clever, clear in debate, and fit for the throat and tongue; he therefore ordered him to issue and receive the king's words and also handle secrets.
idiomatic: Wencheng called Xiu clever and clear in debate, fit for the king's voice; he issued and received words and handled secrets.

literal: On imperial progresses and hunts he attended at the left and right.
idiomatic: On progresses and hunts he attended left and right.

literal: When Xianwen took the throne he was transferred to Palace Attendant and joined the staff of Grand General of the South Murong Baiyao.
idiomatic: When Xianwen took the throne he was Palace Attendant on Baiyao's southern staff.

literal: In the Yansing era the Masters of Writing memorialized that Dunhuang, one garrison, lay far in the northwest on the bandit route and might not hold, and wished to move it to Liangzhou.
idiomatic: In Yansing the Masters of Writing said Dunhuang lay far northwest on the bandit road and might not hold, and wished to move it to Liangzhou.

literal: The ministers met in council; all thought it right.
idiomatic: Ministers met; all agreed.

literal: Xiu alone said: "This is a matter of shrinking the state, not of opening territory.
idiomatic: Xiu alone said, "This shrinks the state; it is not opening territory.

literal: I hold that Dunhuang was established long ago; though neighboring strong bandits, soldiers and people are used to it—routine garrison placement is enough for self-defense.
idiomatic: Dunhuang was long established; though bandits neighbor it, soldiers and people are used to routine garrison—enough for defense.

literal: If moved to Guzang, I fear men will harbor other thoughts, or greed for what they leave in heavy relocation and be unwilling to move.
idiomatic: Moved to Guzang, men may harbor other thoughts, or cling to what they leave and refuse to go.

literal: If bandits are thereby drawn to invade within, it will deeply harm the state.
idiomatic: If that draws bandits inward, the state is deeply harmed.

literal: Moreover, abandoning the far for the near leaves distant defense gaps.
idiomatic: Abandoning the far for the near leaves distant defense gaps.

literal: Once abolished, that awakens the barbarians' hearts; then Yi and Di will intrigue and come and go with each other.
idiomatic: Once abolished, barbarian hearts awaken; Yi and Di intrigue and pass back and forth.

literal: Guanxi will be disturbed in the wild; beacon alarms will not cease; frontier service will multiply and hardship will be great.
idiomatic: Guanxi will run wild; beacons will not cease; frontier service will multiply and hardship grow.

literal: "They followed Xiu's proposal.
idiomatic: They followed Xiu's proposal.

literal: Later he was General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing.
idiomatic: Later he was General Who Pacifies the East and Qing Inspector.

literal: At death his son Wu inherited the rank.
idiomatic: At death son Wu inherited.

literal: Wu, styled Daoshi, was upright and careful and had administrative capacity.
idiomatic: Wu, styled Daoshi, was upright, careful, and capable in administration.

literal: As Chief Administrator of Pacify-the-North in Dingzhou he took many bribes and was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Li Ping.
idiomatic: As Dingzhou Pacify-the-North Chief Administrator he took bribes and was impeached by Censor Li Ping.

literal: Handed to the Court of Justice, he was pardoned when an amnesty came.
idiomatic: Handed to the Court of Justice, he was freed by amnesty.

literal: Later he was made Dragon-Prancing General and Inspector of Ying.
idiomatic: Later he was Dragon-Prancing General and Ying Inspector.

literal: Wu presented a bed of seven treasures and an ivory mat.
idiomatic: Wu presented a seven-treasure bed and ivory mat.

literal: The edict said: "Formerly Jin Emperor Wu burned the pheasant-head robe; I have always praised that.
idiomatic: The edict said, "Jin Emperor Wu burned the pheasant-head robe; I have always praised that.

literal: What Wu now presents is also of that sort.
idiomatic: What Wu presents is of that sort.

literal: Curious and gorgeous things violate plain custom; give them to his household people."
idiomatic: Gorgeous things violate plain custom; give them to his household."

literal: Later for falsely reporting defeating bandits he was dismissed.
idiomatic: Later for falsely reporting bandit victories he was dismissed.

literal: After long time he was made Grand Master of Palace Counsel and advanced to General of the Left; he died.
idiomatic: After long time he was Grand Master of Palace Counsel and General of the Left; he died.

literal: Yao Xuan, styled Bixie, was a man of Changzi in Shangdang.
idiomatic: Yao Xuan, styled Bixie, came from Changzi in Shangdang.

literal: His original name was Zhongkui; later he was granted the name Xuan.
idiomatic: His original name was Zhongkui; later he was granted the name Xuan.

literal: His grandfather Senglai, when Daowu pacified Zhongshan, came to submit to the state with Lü Han of Zhao commandery.
idiomatic: Grandfather Senglai, when Daowu pacified Zhongshan, came to submit with Lü Han of Zhao.

literal: Xuan was clever and had a beautiful countenance.
idiomatic: Xuan was clever and handsome.

literal: He was commander of a thousand-man army.
idiomatic: He was commander of a thousand-man army.

literal: Taiwu for his respectful care promoted him to Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: Taiwu for respectful care promoted him to Palace Attendant.

literal: Later he was also Director of the Northern Department in the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Later he was also Northern Department Director in the Masters of Writing.

literal: At the time the Three Chiefs were first established; Xuan was envoy to the thirteen eastern provinces to revise household registers and was granted one private carriage and four stable horses.
idiomatic: When the Three Chiefs were first established, Xuan was envoy to thirteen eastern provinces to revise registers and was granted a carriage and four stable horses.

literal: Xuan before and after followed campaigns and went out on inspection some thirty times, all with a name for restraining self and serving the public.
idiomatic: Before and after he followed campaigns and inspected some thirty times, all with a name for self-restraint and public service.

literal: Rewards of clothes, colored silk, and slave girls and the like; he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingyang.
idiomatic: Rewarded with clothes, silk, and slaves, he was Baron of Pingyang.

literal: When the hundred offices were reorganized he was made Minister of the Imperial Stud and transferred to Minister of Grain.
idiomatic: When offices were reorganized he was Minister of the Imperial Stud, then Minister of Grain.

literal: He died at Pingcheng.
idiomatic: He died at Pingcheng.

literal: Xiaowen mourned him and posthumously made him Inspector of Xiang.
idiomatic: Xiaowen mourned him and posthumously made him Xiang Inspector.

literal: Earlier, when Xuan reached Xuzhou and saw the commandery towers and belvederes, he disliked their splendor and ordered them torn down here and there; therefore they later fell further into ruin.
idiomatic: Earlier at Xuzhou he disliked the towers' splendor and had them torn down; they fell further into ruin.

literal: When Xiaowen visited Pengcheng and heard of it, he said: "Xuan could still be pursued and beheaded."
idiomatic: When Xiaowen visited Pengcheng he said, "Xuan could still be pursued and beheaded."

literal: Xuan's eldest son Hong inherited the rank.
idiomatic: Eldest son Hong inherited.
